note_add: No park entry fee: the camping fee covers the site and parking for one vehicle (some busy parks need a free day-use pass for day visitors). Camping fees and the non-resident fee include tax; the transaction fees (reservation, change, cancellation, call-centre surcharge) have tax added. The non-resident fee is $20 per party per campground, reserved or first come, and not charged for children or youth. A second vehicle pays 50% of the base camping fee, up to $12 a night; further vehicles are set by the park operator. A camping party is at least one adult (16+), no more than four adults and no more than eight people in all; the fee is per party, not per person. No weekend or holiday premium is published; fees vary by park and by peak season (June 15 to Labour Day).

note_add: No day-use or entry fee in provincial parks, except that vehicles parked at provincial parks and public land sites in Kananaskis Country and the Bow Valley Corridor need a Kananaskis Conservation Pass ($15 a day for one vehicle, $90 a year; trailers and extra passengers free; McLean Creek and Fisher Creek PRAs exempt); camping fees do not include it, and it is on the entries that need it. Fees include GST (Alberta has no PST) unless a campground says otherwise; some concession-run campgrounds post prices before tax. The $12 reservation fee is the same online and by phone; changes are $10 online, $5 per amendment for phone-in reservations. A campsite may hold at most three camping units, motor vehicles and towed equipment in all, only two of them used for sleeping; a second camping fee is charged when both sleeping units are not tents. Each site posts its own maximum number of people.

note_add: Every vehicle in a provincial park needs a park entry permit, charged on top of camping: $11 a day, $42 a week, $82 a year ($45 for an annual bought October 1 to April 30), the same for everyone; free for Saskatchewan residents 65+ and for First Nations, Metis and Inuit people exercising traditional use rights, 25% off with a SaskAbilities accessible parking permit. There is no extra-vehicle camping fee, but a towed car needs its own entry permit. Sask Parks' complete 2026-27 rates and fees table lists no non-resident, extra-person, extra-vehicle, weekend or holiday charge, and its fees include all applicable taxes. Reservation fee $12 online or in park, $14 through the call centre; change and cancellation $15 ($17 by phone).

note_add: Campers need a park vehicle permit on top of the camping fee (the daily permit runs to midnight on the day bought, so a one-night stay touches two days; the three-day permit is $16.50). The Park Fees Regulation sets every fee, GST included: one nightly fee per campsite, with no non-resident, per-person or extra-vehicle charge and no weekend or holiday premium (campgrounds run by private operators set their own). The $10 reservation fee is per stay and facility, online or by phone; changes $4. Six people or one family per site (parents and children under 18, a grandparent allowed); one camping unit, and one vehicle per campsite unless an officer approves more, guests parking in designated areas. Every vehicle needs its own permit; an annual permit can carry two plates.
